title: Structure of the Earth and Geologic Time
seo_title: Grade 9 Science: Structure of the Earth and Geologic Time Worksheets (MATATAG)
short_title: the Earth's layers and geologic time
standard_code: Grade 9, Quarter 2: Earth and Space Science
standard_text: The Earth has layers (crust, mantle, outer core, inner core) studied using seismic waves; the geologic time scale; relative and absolute (radiometric) dating of rocks and fossils. (summary of the MATATAG Science curriculum, Grade 9, Quarter 2: Earth and Space Science)
meta_desc: Free Grade 9 Science worksheets (MATATAG, Quarter 2: Earth and Space Science): the Earth's layers, seismic evidence, dating rocks, the geologic time scale and the fossil record. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Crust, mantle, outer core, inner core.
key_sub: Lower rock layers are usually older.
body_html:
How to think about it

The Earth has a thin solid crust, a thick hot mantle, a liquid outer core and a solid inner core. Scientists learned this from seismic waves: S-waves cannot pass through the liquid outer core.

The geologic time scale divides the Earth's 4.6-billion-year history into eons, eras and periods. Relative dating uses the order of rock layers and fossils; absolute dating uses the half-lives of radioactive isotopes to give ages in years.

Example

Which layer is liquid?

S-waves do not pass

Answer: the outer core

Example

Half-life 5,730 years; 1/4 left. Age?

Two half-lives

Answer: 11,460 years

Common mistakes

  • Thinking the mantle is liquid lava.
  • Thinking relative dating gives an age in years.
  • Thinking humans lived with dinosaurs.

faq.a: From how seismic waves travel and bend through different layers.
A fossil of a species that lived for a short time over a wide area, used to date rock layers.

items.q: Which best describes Earth's mantle?
c: solid iron and nickel under enormous pressure
thin, rocky outer layer; thickest under continents
thick layer of hot solid rock that moves by slow convection
liquid iron and nickel whose motion makes Earth's magnetic field
items.e: Match the layer.

items.q: Evidence: Earth's average density (5.5 g/cm³) is much greater than crust rock (2.7 g/cm³). What does it show?
c: Much denser material, like iron, must be deep inside.
The outer core is a different material and state from the mantle.
items.e: We learn about the interior mainly from seismic waves and density.

A mineral has 1/32 of its original uranium-235 left (half-life 704 million years). How old is it?

items.q: What is a negative feedback loop?
c: a change that triggers effects that reduce the original change
a change that is made larger by its effects
a feedback that always warms Earth
items.e: Negative feedback tends to stabilize a system.

items.q: A sample starts with 200 g of a radioactive parent. How much parent is left after 4 half-lives?

items.e: 1/4 = 2 half-lives; 2 × 704 = 1,408 million years.

items.q: A sample had 200 g of parent and now has 6.25 g. How many half-lives have passed?
items.e: 200 → 6.25 takes 5 halvings.

items.e: Daughter = original − parent left = 64 − 16 = 48 g.

items.q: Rose observes in a cliff: “A fault breaks layers A, B and C but not layer D on top.” What can be concluded?
